executiveSummary: GM1721 passes the complete deterministic contract over all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS identity, generalized boundary, headline demography, 53 neighbourhoods, six BAG places, 23 BRT settlements, eight NWB links, null semantics, local reconciliation, explanation ledgers, exact zero-intensity behavior and sustained-water repair guard are coherent. Release remains correction-required for three spatial-evidence defects. First, the named Rhine, Meuse and IJssel preset produces sustained municipality-wide inundation stress without selecting the real Bernheze pathway: every core drains through Beekgraaf, Kleine/Groote Wetering, Leijgraaf and Aa, while high Maas can back water into the regional system. The generic result reaches internal amplitude 1.637795 at T+12 through T+72 and produces 20,480 modeled people under pressure and 1,210,409 cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours at T+72, despite selecting no EDO 36/Aa scenario, defence, water level, connected footprint, arrival or recession. Second, river and pluvial neighbourhood maps have the identical seeded 53-area ranking rather than the municipality's documented valleys, flat Loosbroek drainage, Rietbeemden high water, Peelland fault and historic channels. Third, a focused synthetic wildfire placed in official neighbourhood Hooge Wijst - De Vorssel, at the Maashorst edge, makes that source neighbourhood rank only seventh while a neighbourhood 9.525 km away ranks fourth; all 53 neighbourhoods receive modeled affected people. The public layer usefully exposes 138 water objects and provider responsibility, but neither causally changes the simulation. All utility views honestly label their shared A50/A59/N279/N324 road flows logical transfer proxies. Physical Brabant Water, Enexis, municipal sewer, telecom, care, food/fuel and emergency-supply topology, live state, backups, stocks, crews and restoration commitments remain unavailable or security-sensitive and were not invented.

evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025 — filtered municipality row GM1721
supports: Official-context GM1721/Bernheze identity, population 32,606 and density 363 residents per square kilometre.
Official age-65-plus count 7,529, equivalent to the generated rounded share 23.1%, and 3,993 one-person households.
The OData table is machine-readable, updated annually and published under CC BY 4.0; rounded or suppressed neighbourhood values require explicit null and reconciliation semantics.

evidenceSources.publisher: PDOK / Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek
evidenceSources.title: Gemeente gegeneraliseerd 2025
supports: Official annual CC BY 4.0 generalized GM1721 polygon consumed by the application.
Municipality-centre point-in-polygon validation and the administrative polygon used for neighbourhood, place and public-asset intersections.

The generalized CBS boundary is not a drainage catchment, flood extent, forest/fire perimeter, provider territory or service area; independently versioned BAG/BRT features retain their own provenance.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Brabant-Noord / Gemeente Vught official council portal
evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel Brabant-Noord 2024–2027
supports: The regional worst-case flood is high Maas/EDO 36, while the profile separately identifies Aa, Dommel and Dieze regional barriers and explicitly warns that local scenario likelihood and impact differ from the regional worst case.

The profile's forest/heath reference is a 200-hectare fire during extreme drought, very strong wind and difficult access; town centres are not directly threatened in that reference and vegetation, accessibility and response matter.

It covers extreme rain, storm, heat, drought, winter conditions, energy and gas loss, drinking-water loss, wastewater-treatment loss, telecom/ICT and cyber-related disruption, and identifies cascading dependencies.

Its essential-service reference durations are 8 hours to 6 days for electricity/gas, drinking water and wastewater treatment and 48 hours for regional telecom/ICT, supporting the 72-hour horizon but not any exact GM1721 curve.
This is a four-year strategic PDF, not a live warning, probability feed, machine event footprint, asset inventory or restoration commitment; no explicit dataset redistribution licence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: Programma Water en Riolering 2024–2027
supports: Every Bernheze core drains toward the Aa through local systems including Beekgraaf, Kleine/Groote Wetering and Leijgraaf; high Maas can cause backwater and regional flooding in Bernheze.

Heeswijk-Dinther is bounded by Aa and Leijgraaf valleys used for temporary storage; Heesch and Nistelrode include high sand and Peelland-fault groundwater pathways; flat Loosbroek has complex polder-like drainage; Vorstenbosch depends on Leijgraaf and Rietbeemden records the highest local water levels; from September 2023 to March 2024 the (ground)water level rose at a rate not seen since national measurements began in 1906.

The detailed inventory reports 211.052 km gravity sewer, 7.5 km force main excluding pressure sewer, 4.124 km drainage, 14.258 km IT/DIT sewer, 18 dry and 23 wet pumping facilities, 778 mechanical-sewer pump units, 322.89 km managed watercourses and 827 culverts/small structures.

Heesch, Nistelrode and Loosbroek wastewater goes to RWZI Vinkel; Vorstenbosch and Heeswijk-Dinther goes to RWZI Dinther. About one third of the stated annual flow is rainwater, creating a concrete drainage/wastewater dependency.

The municipality uses a 2021 climate stress test, climate substrate map and groundwater-monitoring work. The public PDF is authoritative planning/inventory context, but no licensed native stress-test GIS, hydraulic connectivity, telemetry, live state or fixed machine update cadence is exposed.

evidenceSources.title: Door droogte zetten we weer tijdelijk gezuiverd afvalwater in
supports: Low Leijgraaf flow triggered temporary use of treated effluent from RWZI Heeswijk-Dinther via Hazelbergse Loop to sustain Wambergse Beek and nearby ditches.
The intervention changes water quality: the water was unsuitable for livestock drinking and recreation until normal flow returned.
This is a dated official observed operational context and demonstrates water/wastewater/ecology coupling; it is not a live API, forecast, full Bernheze network state or recurring licensed dataset.

evidenceSources.title: Memo natuurbrandbeheersing in Noord-Brabant
supports: The Maashorst/Reekerheide nature-fire area commission explicitly relates to Bernheze, Oss, Maashorst and Land van Cuijk.
VRBN identifies topography, meteorology and vegetation as the fire-behaviour triangle, and cites accessibility, escape routes, dry-period simultaneous fires and suppressive capacity as material.
RIN is used professionally for advice, but this memo is a policy PDF; it supplies no public bulk perimeter/fuel API, licence, fixed refresh cadence or local first-72-hour resource state.

evidenceSources.title: Nationaal Wegenbestand Wegen OGC API
supports: Machine-readable road-section geometry underlying GM1721's eight A50/A59/N279/N324 cross-boundary logical routes.
The OGC service declares monthly updates and CC0 1.0; a dated snapshot remains necessary because the service is mutable.
NWB contains static road geometry and identity, not current closure, congestion, emergency access, evacuation throughput or electricity, water, drainage, gas, telecom, facility or supply capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards via PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Waterschappen Kunstwerken IMWA and Waterketen DAMO OGC APIs
supports: Machine-readable object-level official context; the current generalized-boundary intersection contains 138 objects: 129 weirs, five sewer pumps, three surface-water pumps and RWZI Dinther.

Kunstwerken IMWA and companion Waterketen DAMO at https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 are CC BY-SA 4.0; Kunstwerken metadata declares weekly updates, while contributor/collection completeness and object timestamps vary.
Five public sewer pumps and one RWZI cannot be treated as the complete 18 dry, 23 wet and 778 mechanical municipal pumping inventory in E04 because source ownership and scopes differ.

The collection is official-context, partial and affectsSimulation=false; object presence/status does not prove hydraulic connectivity, controls, emergency power, live availability or restoration time.

regionalDetail.summary: All 53 neighbourhoods expose broad aggregate context, but suppressions remain null and these fields do not locate individual need or physical hazard.
notes: Address density, ages, households, businesses, cars, homes, housing form/tenure, benefit indicators, doctor/supermarket distance, land/water and urbanity are available in all 53 neighbourhoods; cars per household is available in 52/53.
District-heating percentage and public-charging-point count are unavailable in all 53 and correctly remain null rather than zero.

The municipality's 23.1% older-resident share and rural distance/car variables are useful aggregate allocation context, not individual dependency, vehicle availability, household preparedness or evacuation observation.
Compound T+24 local population, affected people and all eight service demand/delivery totals reconcile exactly to the municipality frame.

settlements.summary: Six BAG woonplaatsen and 23 BRT settlements remain distinct from CBS administration; Vinkel exposes a documented geometry-edition caveat.
notes: The six active BAG places are Heesch, Heeswijk-Dinther, Loosbroek, Nistelrode, Vinkel and Vorstenbosch; BRT contributes 23 labels: 14 buurtschappen, one deelkern, three gehuchten and five woonkernen.

The Vinkel BAG label centre [5.489900357858788, 51.70530532030259] falls outside the independently versioned generalized CBS municipality polygon. This is a label/generalization mismatch, not evidence that the intersecting BAG place is invalid.
E04 also names RWZI Vinkel as a wastewater destination, so settlement labels and utility nodes must not be inferred from one another.
Neither BAG/BRT units nor the label point is substituted for official GM1721 population or the 53 CBS neighbourhoods.

transport.summary: Eight NWB routes and scheduled stops are structurally valid, but capacities are generalized and no live access state is present.
notes: A50/A59/N279/N324 routes connect Oss, Maashorst, 's-Hertogenbosch, Meierijstad and Sint-Michielsgestel; all endpoints resolve. Segment lengths are 0.919, 3.718, 4.112, 3.636, 1.466, 0.107, 2.392 and 0.627 km.
Five motorway links use nominal capacity 260 and three regional links 150, totaling 1,750 scenario units in every service view. These values are not road throughput or utility capacity.
No ProRail station lies inside the boundary; 40 GTFS stop areas are present as scheduled/static context.
No NDW incident/closure, congestion, bridge/culvert passability, emergency route, evacuation throughput, vehicle availability or repair-access state drives the first 72 hours.

emergencyContext.summary: Authoritative sources establish local water, wastewater, nature-fire, vulnerability and vital-process dependencies that the generic model does not causally encode.
notes: E04 locates distinct water pathways and two wastewater destinations and inventories hundreds of assets; E05 demonstrates a real drought-time RWZI-to-surface-water intervention and water-quality restriction.

E03/E06 make accessibility, vegetation, wind, reduced self-reliance and electricity/telecom/water/wastewater cascades relevant, but do not supply current incident footprints or local operational resources.

The current public provider lookup at the municipal reference point resolves Enexis for electricity/gas, Brabant Water for drinking water and Ziggo for fixed-media context; drainage coverage is absent and provider polygons are non-causal.
The current public context intersection contains 138 water objects and zero government-service locations. Neither count proves absence/completeness or affects simulation.
No sensitive/operational topology, facility role/capacity, backup, stock, crew, fuel or restoration commitment was inferred.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets completed at all six required checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: Peak municipality severities were storm 0.560738, pluvial 0.308231, river 0.506785, coastal 0, heat 0.459917, winter 0.564401, cyber 0.414900, earthquake 0.009841, wildfire 0.143799 and compound 0.823698.

At T+24 compound had rain 47.636919 mm/h, inundation-stress amplitude 0.232682, wind 28.087920 m/s, cyber disruption 0.363991, system pressure 0.691053, 25,314 modeled people under pressure and 271,299 cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours.

At T+72 compound retained inundation-stress amplitude 0.232682 and cyber disruption 0.047341, with severity 0.298380, pressure 0.694153, 25,456 people under pressure and 1,096,929 cumulative proxy person-hours.
apps/web/src/scenarios.ts clones canonical sim-core presets. All values are deterministic derived scenario estimates, not observed Bernheze weather, probability, incident or outage data.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact no-event semantics, determinism, monotonic cumulative burden, route bounds and local reconciliation pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1721 pnpm audit:model passed both tests across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services in 33.85 seconds on the initial focused run.
Every canonical preset at intensity zero produced exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every checkpoint.
Repeated frames are deterministic; state is finite/bounded; cumulative person-hours are monotonic; and route flow never exceeds effective logical capacity.
Compound T+24 local allocation reconciles municipality population 32,606, affected population 25,314 and all eight demand/delivery balances, with maximum floating-point discrepancy 1.07e-14.
Changing among all eleven map layers leaves hazard, system pressure and affected population exactly invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The generic main-river field and shared seeded neighbourhood order do not represent Bernheze's water systems, terrain, forests or explicit event source.
notes: River inundation stress rises from zero at T+0 to 0.576504 at T+6 and 1.637795 at T+12, remaining 1.637795 through T+72; affected population is 10,572 at T+12, 16,992 at T+24 and 20,480 at T+48/T+72.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-461 derives river exposure from municipality-centre distance to three coarse diagonal segments; lines 642-647 apply a scalar without a selected EDO 36/Aa footprint, water level, defence, arrival or recession layer.

E03 says regional and local scenario impact differ; E04 documents the actual Aa/Leijgraaf/Beekgraaf/Wetering/Peelland-fault and Maas-backwater mechanisms. None causes the generic municipality-wide scalar.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3377-3390 applies municipality severity multiplied by one deterministic region seed. River and pluvial therefore have the identical exact ranking across all 53 neighbourhoods: Componistenbuurt, Menzel, Kennedystraat and Heilige Stok - Kerkstraat lead both.

At pluvial T+24 Loosbroek ranks 35/53, Heische Wal - DintherseHoek 40/53 and the source-documented local water areas are not selected by a stress-test cell, surface, stream, sewer, elevation or fault input. The result is reproducible synthetic allocation, not a validation against E04.

In a focused synthetic T+24 wildfire with source [5.552221405163929, 51.72449837556086] at the centre of BU17210403 Hooge Wijst - De Vorssel on the Maashorst edge, the containing neighbourhood ranks 7/53 at 0.547883 while BU17210203 Heilige Stok - Kerkstraat ranks fourth at 0.553944 despite its centre being 9.525 km away. Every neighbourhood receives modeled affected people. The local order exactly repeats the river/pluvial seed order.
Coastal direct inundation remains exactly zero, correctly separating no local coastal water from the preset's wind-only indirect service stress.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight service balances and dependencies are inspectable, but their magnitudes are not calibrated to Bernheze assets, providers, villages or catchments.
notes: River T+24 availability was power 0.795634, water 0.235851, drainage 0.630829, gas 0.545266, telecom 0.201930, mobility 0.521452, facilities 0.707416 and supply 0.217729.
Compound T+24 availability was power 0.498434, water 0.163538, drainage 0.170250, gas 0.362081, telecom 0.123943, mobility 0.262443, facilities 0.165624 and supply 0.657813.

E03 supports the direction of vital-process cascades and E04/E05 support drainage/wastewater/surface-water coupling, but no source calibrates these exact availability, demand, delivery or repair values.

The causal graph has no named Aa/Leijgraaf catchment, public weir/pump, municipal sewer subsystem, RWZI Vinkel/Dinther edge, Brabant Water zone, Enexis station, telecom site, emergency facility role, depot or village stock node.
All eight service views reuse the same eight NWB-derived routes and nominal total 1,750; emitted transferSemantics is consistently logical-proxy at packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:2011-2014.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality explanation ledgers close and preserve scenario confidence, controls, dependency ordering and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; each service baseline plus exact-stage deltas sums to availability; all eight weighted service-pressure contributions sum to municipality system pressure.
Dependency chains, drivers, local vulnerability/demand factors, recovery progress and service-restoration counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.
Household preparedness changes modeled people/supply consequences after physical pressure rather than changing physical hazard fragility.
Operational controls and time-gated interventions are labeled scenario assumptions; shared road-derived utility flows remain logical proxies.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours integrate weighted unmet-service pressure against a matched no-event baseline and are not observed customer outage-hours, casualties, displacement or welfare loss.

recovery72h.summary: Sustained-water and response-delay safeguards behave consistently, but unsupported forcing and absent resource/state inputs prevent operational recovery interpretation.
notes: River forcing remains active at T+72, all eight service recovery-progress values remain exactly zero, pressure is 0.585804, 20,480 people remain under pressure and cumulative proxy burden reaches 1,210,409 person-hours.
River T+72 keeps seven service availabilities at their T+24 values while facilities declines from 0.707416 to 0.165222 through generic dependencies; this is not a local care/operator forecast.
Pluvial water clears by T+48 and T+72 pressure falls to 0.046354 with no affected population; recovery progress reaches 0.952329–1. Compound retains 0.232682 generic water and zero recovery at T+72.
Ended storm, winter, wildfire and earthquake forcing recovers monotonically; the two-week heatwave and cyber schedule retain bounded forcing through T+72.
Actual surface-water levels, drainage operation, provider switching, road access, crews, mutual aid, fuel, spares, staffing, stock and restoration estimates are unknown.

findings.summary: A coarse proximity corridor creates unsupported sustained Rhine/Meuse/IJssel inundation instead of a selected Bernheze Aa/Maas-backwater scenario.
findings.evidence: E03 defines high Maas/EDO 36 as a regional worst case but explicitly notes local scenarios differ and separately identifies Aa/Dommel/Dieze regional systems. E04 says every Bernheze core drains through named smaller waters toward Aa and that high Maas can back up the Bernheze system. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-461 nevertheless measures the GM1721 centroid against three coarse diagonal segments, and lines 642-647 turn that screen into water. The canonical preset emits inundation-stress amplitude 0.576504 at T+6 and 1.637795 at T+12 through T+72, with 16,992 modeled people/302,702 event-attributable service person-hours at T+24 and 20,480 people/1,210,409 person-hours at T+72. No EDO 36 or Aa scenario, defence, water level, connected footprint, arrival or recession supports that magnitude. This is municipality-specific evidence of a shared national proximity-field defect, not a claim that Bernheze lacks high-water risk.
findings.action: Mark GM1721's current direct named-major-river result unsupported/Unknown and numerically neutral in downstream decisions until an expert-selected connected footprint exists; explicitly preserve Aa, Leijgraaf, Wetering, groundwater, regional-barrier and Maas-backwater mechanisms as unresolved rather than safe. The durable fix must intersect a named/versioned LIWO or Aa en Maas scenario and expose people/services only within an approved hydraulic footprint.

findings.summary: One seeded neighbourhood order replaces Bernheze's documented mechanism-specific rainwater, valley, fault and drainage geography.
findings.evidence: E04 distinguishes Aa/Leijgraaf valleys at Heeswijk-Dinther, flat polder-like Loosbroek, Leijgraaf/Rietbeemden at Vorstenbosch, Beekgraaf/Groote Wetering and Peelland-fault water at Nistelrode, and Heesch's east-west Wetering path. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3377-3390 instead applies one hazardSeed multiplier to municipality severity. River and pluvial therefore have the identical exact 53-neighbourhood order, beginning Componistenbuurt, Menzel, Kennedystraat and Heilige Stok - Kerkstraat. At pluvial T+24 Loosbroek ranks 35/53, while no official stress-test cell, sewer, watercourse, elevation, soil/fault or asset state is sampled. The ranking is reproducible synthetic allocation, not validation against E04.
findings.action: Mark neighbourhood direct-water distribution unsupported until a versioned source layer is supplied. Obtain the native GIS behind the municipality's climate stress test/substrate map and/or a matching Klimaateffectatlas water-depth grid, preserve event/return period, cell size, unit, edition, no-data and uncertainty, and use AHN/IMWA/GWSW only as disclosed covariates. Add fixtures proving river and pluvial footprints can differ and approved source cells—not a hash—govern local direct impact.

findings.summary: An explicit Maashorst-edge wildfire source does not control the neighbourhood map shown for local impact.
findings.evidence: E03 limits its reference direct fire to forest/heath rather than town centres; E06 explicitly connects Bernheze to Maashorst/Reekerheide and identifies topography, weather, vegetation, accessibility and suppression as causal. A focused synthetic scenario placed the source at [5.552221405163929, 51.72449837556086], the official centre of BU17210403 Hooge Wijst - De Vorssel. At T+24 the municipality has direct-fire intensity 0.435024, smoke 0.526836, severity 0.475597, pressure 0.191540 and 2,368 modeled people under pressure, but the source neighbourhood ranks only 7/53 at 0.547883; BU17210203 Heilige Stok - Kerkstraat ranks fourth at 0.553944 despite its centre being 9.525 km away. All 53 neighbourhoods receive affected people and the order exactly matches river/pluvial because packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3377-3390 never uses local source intersection/distance. This is a synthetic reproducibility test, not evidence of a current fire.
findings.action: Until polygon-aware local fire allocation exists, label neighbourhood fire-impact distribution synthetic/unsupported and do not use its rank for deployment. Prefer an authorized NIPV Risiko-index Natuurbranden export; otherwise combine BRT TOP10NL land cover, timestamped KNMI weather/fuel-moisture proxies and an explicit source/perimeter with visibly scenario-based spread assumptions. Tests must prioritize source-intersecting eligible forest cells and expose flame, smoke, fuel, wind, access and suppression separately.

findings.summary: The public water layer is useful context but incomplete and non-causal for first-72-hour drainage and wastewater performance.
findings.evidence: E08 contributes 129 weirs, five sewer pumps, three surface-water pumps and RWZI Dinther inside the generalized boundary. E04 separately inventories 18 dry and 23 wet pumping facilities, 778 mechanical-sewer pump units, 211.052 km gravity sewer, 322.89 km municipal watercourses and 827 culverts/small structures, and routes villages to RWZI Vinkel or Dinther. These ownership/scopes cannot be reconciled as a complete public network, and the application correctly marks public assets affectsSimulation=false. The pluvial T+24 municipality is mobility-limited at availability 0.507241; drainage state and its T+48/T+72 recovery likewise come from generic equations, not connectivity, pumps, overflow/storage, RWZI state, emergency power or telemetry.
findings.action: Retain IMWA/DAMO/GWSW objects as partial non-causal context. Request a licensed, security-reviewed municipal GWSW/hydraulic topology and exercise state; only then add village/catchment-to-pump/storage/RWZI dependencies. Where data cannot be released, offer bounded named drainage-subsystem scenarios with explicit pump, telemetry, backup and capacity assumptions rather than inferring function from public points.

findings.summary: Eight road corridors are cloned across all services and cannot represent Bernheze physical utility or response topology.
findings.evidence: E07 supports A50/A59/N279/N324 geometry and monthly identity updates only. The model applies the same eight links and nominal total 1,750 to power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply. E03/E04 instead establish service-specific provision areas, two RWZI destinations and cascading dependencies. The engine/UI correctly emit transferSemantics logical-proxy, but road direction, nominal capacity and flow are not cables, pipes, radio backhaul, patient transfers or food/fuel routes.
findings.action: Keep the logical-proxy label and prevent these flows from supporting physical claims. Add service-specific edges only from authorized topology or an explicitly named exercise gateway; preserve Unknown capacity/state. Use NWB plus timestamped NDW only for mobility/repair-access context and never clone road capacity into utilities.

findings.summary: Provider responsibility and aggregate vulnerability are known, but facility, household and supply continuity are not operationally resolved.
findings.evidence: E01 establishes 7,529 residents aged 65+ and 3,993 one-person households; E03 warns that reduced self-reliance and extended service failures matter. The public provider lookup returns Enexis electricity/gas, Brabant Water and Ziggo at the reference point, while the current government-service snapshot intersects zero points. No evidence establishes care roles, beds, staffing, household medical electricity need, supermarkets/pharmacies, food/water/fuel stocks, depots, vehicles, backup runtime, priority customers or restoration agreements. Facilities and supply outputs are therefore synthetic planning balances, not operational inventories.
findings.action: Retain aggregate context without individual scoring. Integrate public BAG/LRK/DUO/ROAZ/Disaster-relevant service registries only where licence, freshness, role and coverage are explicit, and seek authorized municipal/GHOR continuity plans for operational roles. Keep capacity, occupancy, stock, backup and dispatch Unknown unless supplied for an exercise.

findings.summary: Weather, cyber, earthquake and remote-wildfire presets are exercises rather than Bernheze observations or local probabilities.
findings.evidence: E03 supports storm, heat, drought, winter weather, wildfire, high-water, vital-service and cyber-related scenarios. The canonical wildfire uses a remote source and yields zero direct flame at GM1721 but smoke 0.346929/drought 0.620113 at T+24; the focused local case is separately unsupported. The canonical Groningen earthquake peaks at only 0.009841 local severity; cyber is a configured target process; all weather values are generated envelopes. No KNMI warning/nowcast, earthquake record, operator incident or Bernheze calibration drives these frames, and the ten presets omit hazardous-material, aviation and public-health risks in E03.
findings.action: Keep all presets clearly labeled synthetic. For live/context mode, ingest timestamped KNMI Open Data observations/forecasts and earthquake catalogue with dataset licence/validity retained; require a selected epicentre and ground-motion model for earthquake. Keep cyber and omitted risk types as explicit exercise inputs until authorized incident/scenario evidence exists.

findings.summary: The Vinkel BAG label/generalized-boundary mismatch must not become a false place or infrastructure exclusion.
findings.evidence: The application intersects six BAG place geometries with GM1721, but the Vinkel label centre [5.489900357858788, 51.70530532030259] lies outside the separately versioned generalized CBS boundary. E04 also names RWZI Vinkel as a service destination, which is a utility relationship independent of whether a place label is inside. The context gate correctly reports the mismatch as a review flag instead of dropping or reassigning the place.
findings.action: Retain polygon-intersection, edition and generalization semantics; never use a place label point to decide municipal membership or service connectivity. Recheck after each CBS/BAG snapshot and model external RWZI nodes from explicit topology only.

findings.summary: Identity, demography, boundary, neighbourhood, place, settlement and public-asset provenance are inspectable and null-safe.
findings.evidence: E01/E02 match GM1721, Bernheze, 32,606 residents, density 363, age-65-plus 7,529 and one-person households 3,993. All 53 neighbourhoods, six BAG places and 23 BRT settlements resolve; the one-person neighbourhood rounding difference is disclosed. Missing district heat/public charging and the one unavailable cars-per-household cell remain null. E08 objects retain source/type/status/timestamp fields and affectsSimulation=false.
findings.action: Retain edition, retrieval, licence, coverage and null semantics; refresh annually or at source cadence and rerun the focused/national gates after each snapshot.

findings.summary: The full deterministic, causal and layer-invariance contract passes for Bernheze.
findings.evidence: The mandatory harness passes 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services; zero-intensity output is exact zero; local compound T+24 population/affected/service balances reconcile; ledgers close; person-hours are matched no-event essential-service pressure; all eleven layer selections preserve simulation state; and every route says logical-proxy.
findings.action: Retain these assertions as regression gates while adding authoritative spatial adapters; do not weaken deterministic or exact-zero behavior to hide calibration gaps.

corrections.summary: Stop exposing Bernheze's generic named-major-river proximity value as supported local inundation and require a selected Aa/Maas-backwater scenario.
corrections.validation: Interim: set GM1721 direct named-major-river spatialEvidence to unsupported, expose the local result as Unknown and make unsupported forcing numerically neutral downstream; state that Aa, Leijgraaf, Wetering, regional-barrier, groundwater and Maas-backwater effects remain unresolved rather than safe. Re-run pnpm test plus focused and ALL municipality gates. residualLimitations: The simulator is a deterministic planning stress test, not a KNMI forecast, warning, probability estimate, live incident picture, casualty model or operator outage forecast.
No approved GM1721 LIWO/Aa en Maas depth, arrival, duration, defence, backwater, runoff, groundwater or catchment grid is ingested; internal inundation stress is not measured local metres.

Marking unsupported Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing Unknown must not erase actual Aa, Leijgraaf, Beekgraaf, Kleine/Groote Wetering, regional-barrier, Peelland-fault, groundwater, sewer-overload or Maas-backwater mechanisms.

The municipal 2021 climate stress test and climate substrate map are described in a planning PDF; their native machine surface, exact event definition, resolution, licence and current validity are not loaded.
CBS neighbourhoods and deterministic seeds do not resolve buildings, terrain depressions, forests, fuels, streams, culverts, sewers, pumps, households, visitors or individual vulnerability.

The public Waterschapshuis layer is intentionally partial; 138 intersecting objects cannot be interpreted as Bernheze's complete 211.052 km sewer/819-pump/322.89 km watercourse/827-culvert system or as operational state.

Provider polygons identify responsibility at one reference point, not full physical coverage, topology or state; drainage may be absent and fixed-media provider areas do not represent mobile coverage.

No physical Brabant Water, Enexis, municipal wastewater, telecom, care or emergency-supply topology, current state, backup, priority-customer list, crew, fuel, spare or restoration estimate is available to the model.
All eight intermunicipal service layers reuse NWB-derived logical corridors and cannot be interpreted as cables, pipes, pressure zones, radio backhaul, patient transfers or food routes.
Static NWB and GTFS inputs do not establish live closure, timetable/vehicle operation, congestion, evacuation throughput or repair access; no railway station lies inside GM1721.
Facilities and supply lack verified care roles, beds, staff, acceptance, care-home occupancy, pharmacies, supermarket/warehouse stock, depots, vehicles and continuity agreements.

Wildfire lacks a local incident perimeter, current fuel/moisture condition, wind-aware spread, suppression state and resource access; the focused Hooge Wijst - De Vorssel case is explicitly synthetic.
Earthquake lacks a selected local event, ground-motion surface, site response and asset fragility; the canonical Groningen event does not test a local Bernheze earthquake.
Generic preparedness, demand, backup, network, repair and intervention multipliers are transparent scenario controls rather than observed Bernheze resources or commitments.

Six-hour checkpoints can miss cloudbursts, flash runoff, dispatch and restrictions; the 72-hour horizon excludes prolonged displacement, contamination, public health, economic loss and reconstruction.
The ten canonical presets omit hazardous-material, aviation, public-health and other risks identified by E03.
